signature_alert.description: Possible SSH brute force attack detected.

analysis.incident_summary: SSH brute force attempt detected from internal host 192.168.0.108 to 192.168.0.109. Host is up but all ports are filtered. High severity with risk score 95.

traffic_analysis.packet_observation: Repeated SSH authentication attempts detected, likely brute force, no successful login observed.

nmap_analysis.security_observation: All ports filtered, indicating potential firewall or IDS blocking. No open services detected, but brute force attempts indicate attacker probing for credentials.

analysis.impact_analysis: Potential compromise of SSH service if credentials are compromised, leading to lateral movement, data exfiltration, or further attacks. Immediate remediation required.
recommendations: Block source IP 192.168.0.108 at firewall level.
Harden SSH: disable root login, enforce key-based authentication, enable fail2ban or similar.
Review system logs for any successful logins or suspicious activity.
Conduct internal scan for other malicious activity or compromised hosts.
Update firewall rules to block brute force attempts and monitor for repeated authentication failures.
analysis.soc_conclusion: The incident demonstrates an internal brute force attack targeting SSH on a critical host. Despite all ports being filtered, the attacker attempted repeated logins, indicating reconnaissance and credential theft attempts. Immediate containment and hardening are essential.
